stories.headline: Cabinet clears hydropower, urban asset policies; approves fruit mandis
stories.title: Cabinet clears hydropower, urban asset policies; approves fruit mandis
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 13: The cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, on Friday approved two major policies on hydropower development and urban asset monetisation, besides clearing land allotments for fruit mandis at Pattan, Tral, and Kulgam and 32 kanals for a grid station in north Kashmir's Bandipora district. The meeting was the first full-strength cabinet sitting in Jammu following the induction of four ministers on October 27. The Office of the Chief Minister, J&K, said in a post on X that Chief Minister Omar Abdullah chaired a meeting of the Council of Ministers in Jammu, deliberating on key proposals aimed at strengthening public welfare, accelerating equitable development and advancing transparent, responsive and effective governance across Jammu and Kashmir. According to sources, the cabinet approved the Jammu and Kashmir Hydropower Policy-2026, which seeks to attract private investment in hydropower projects with a capacity of up to 100 MW under the Independent Power Producer (IPP) and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models. The cabinet also cleared the Urban Asset Mapping and Monetisation Policy-2026, prepared by the Housing and Urban Development Department. The policy aims to identify, map, and optimise the use of assets owned by Urban Local Bodies across Jammu and Kashmir to generate additional revenue for strengthening civic infrastructure and improving public services. In another decision, sources said the cabinet approved the e-auction of the SumchamPadder mineral block in Kishtwar district through the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, to grant an exploration licence for copper, nickel, and associated mineralisation. They said that the cabinet also approved transferring 32 kanals of Shamilat land at Nadikhai and Poshwari in the Hajin area of Bandipora district to the Power Development Department for constructing a grid station. The proposed grid station is expected to strengthen the electricity distribution network in the area. In a move aimed at strengthening agricultural marketing infrastructure, the cabinet cleared land allotment proposals for establishing fruit mandis at Pattan, Tral and Kulgam, the sources said. The proposed facilities are expected to provide marketing infrastructure to fruit growers and facilitate the trade and transportation of agricultural produce. Cabinet Minister Javed Ahmad Rana said proposals concerning land required for power projects being developed under the PPP model, agricultural and fruit markets, and the Subsidiary Intelligence Bureau were taken up at the meeting. He said certain promotion-related cases were considered. Rana said the regularisation of daily wagers was not discussed and did not figure on the cabinet agenda. The issue remains a longstanding demand of dailywagers and other temporary workers employed in various government departments across Jammu and Kashmir. The rehabilitation of traders affected by fires at Jammu's Warehouse Market and Shiv Market was also not discussed at the meeting, Rana said. Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Kumar Choudhary and ministers Ali Mohammad Sagar, Sakeena Itoo, Javed Ahmad Rana, Javid Ahmad Dar, Mir Saifullah, Shamim Firdous, and Altaf Ahmad Wani attended the meeting. The cabinet expansion on October 27 brought four new ministers — Ali Mohammad Sagar, Mir Saifullah, Shamim Firdous and Altaf Ahmad Wani - into the Council of Ministers, taking its strength to the maximum permissible nine, including the Chief Minister. Satish Sharma was dropped in the reshuffle.
